Diego,

We started seeing a large P95 latency jump and increased 5xx rate across our inference endpoint around 08:45 PDT this morning right after we received the v5q modelpack push (you folks indicated the q-profile would be live by 07:50).

Symptoms:
- p95 baseline ~0.45s → spike to ~2.4s for consumer text generation requests
- 5xx rate increased from ~0.1% to ~3.7%
- Throughput throttling on our 50rps lane (errors + retries causing backpressure)
- A handful of production responses contain incorrect account references (sensitive hallucinations) — attached one transcript and screenshot.

This is customer-facing and we have multiple merchants actively impacted. Can you confirm whether Redwood did a q-profile flip or any config change tied to v5q this morning? We need an urgent mitigation path and an ETA.

--
Ethan Walker

Subject: Re: OceanGate: sustained stressburst and response incoherence after q-profile upgrade

Diego / team — initial triage notes (attaching metric + log snippets): qprofile-v5q-metrics.csv, svc-logs-snippet.txt.

What I see so far:
- Strong temporal correlation: v5q q-profile began serving for OceanGate at 07:49:43 PDT. Latency and 5xx spikes begin ~07:58–08:10 window.
- Higher token-decode CPU jitter on the GPU host; memory pressure events and KV-cache evictions are elevated in the same timeframe.
- Error signatures show more token-generation truncation + decoder timeouts (mapped to our new int8-gptq path).
- A small subset of prompts with long instruction+context windows are triggering attention-kernel path divergence (we see different kernel selection vs. v4safe). This explains both latency and the coherence/hallucination regressions for long-context cases.

Hypothesis: the v5q q-profile uses an aggressive int8 quant path that, on sequences >1024 tokens for this tenant's workload distribution, causes degraded decoding latency and sporadic coherence failures (likely due to rtol/atol differences in quant steps and a fallback that truncates generation).

Immediate mitigations we can take (ordered by impact):
A) Roll back OceanGate’s model pack to v5fp32 (safe) — fastest path to restore latency/quality.
B) Flip their q-profile to the "v4safe" config (less aggressive quant) — medium impact, lower perf loss than full rollback.
C) Apply a per-tenant max_seq clamp to 1024 to avoid the attention kernel path for now (works but may truncate expected responses).

I recommend A -> validate -> monitor. If we do rollback, plan: 11:30 rollback, 11:45 smoke test on a canary, 12:00 monitor p95/5xx and customer lane throughput; provide customer update 12:30. I’ve included a short rollback-plan.md in the incident drive.

I’ll stand by on the bridge.

— Irene Choi
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime — Redwood Inference
